text: Attempt 10: attempt 4's fast start (big early zoning, low tax, early loans) carried past 30,000 by fixing what killed every fast attempt - debt (raise taxes while demand is at max), fire (station per block), wiring/water/traffic, unlocks before caps. From the reflection on all 9 attempts.

Reflection across all nine attempts: population follows home land zoned early (about 20 people per home tile). The three fast attempts had 565-650 home tiles by 2005, low starting tax and 4-6 early loans; every cautious attempt stalled under 12,000. Attempt 10 copies the fast start and fixes what killed each fast attempt.
Block 1 ($11,055): road + rail links, coal plant, 108 light homes, 72 factory, 36 shop tiles, 6 riverbank pumps, fire station
Taxes homes 5%, shops 4%, factories 4%; parking fines on
Loan #2 for block 2 (home demand at max, plan schedule)
Block 2 ($9,258): south homes/shops/factories, fire and police stations, second coal plant, 6 riverbank pumps
Controller fix: police stations use tile 0xD2, which the power-plant range wrongly included (build check missed the station; audit could treat it as a power source). Range corrected
Loan #3 for block 3 and a pump field: home and factory demand at max; growth tracks empty zoned land
Block 3 ($2,938): east homes, shops, factory strip x110-114, 60 home tiles y36-40; 19 north riverbank pumps ($2,550)
Audit stopped the clock: the east factory strip's power column only touched empty zones. Linked across road x=108 at built factories (y47, y52); joined the split water main
Growth tracks empty zoned land: the game builds on a steady share of empty zoned tiles each month, so more zoned land means faster growth. Block 3 adds ~230 home tiles and a large factory strip.
Block 4 ($4,572 from cash): south district y56-76, 264 home tiles, 108 factory, 36 shop; land nearly full, all demand at max
